```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
```



```{r setup}
library(ProfileGLMM)

data("exposure_data")
exp_data = exposure_data$df
head(exp_data)
```



Here we work with the simulated dataset presented in the introduction vignette and set up the model in the same way:



```{r}
covList = {}
covList$FE = c('X')

covList$RE = c('t')
covList$REunit = c('indiv')

covList$Lat = c('X')

covList$Assign$Cont = c('Exp1','Exp2')
covList$Assign$Cat = NULL

covList$Y = c('Y')
dataProfile = profileGLMM_preprocess(regType = 'linear',
                                     covList = covList,
                                     dataframe = exp_data,
                                     nC = 30,
                                     intercept = list(FE = T, RE = F, Lat = T))
print(dataProfile)
```



The `profileGLMM_preprocess()` function creates the quantities needed to sample from the posterior using `profileGLMM_Gibbs()`. Alongside the design matrices and model metadata, it sets default weakly informative priors in the `$prior` element:



```{r}
print(dataProfile$prior)
```



Using these initial priors, `profileGLMM_preprocess()` draws starting values for the MCMC chain and stores them in `$theta`:



```{r}
print(dataProfile$theta)
```



## Setting Custom Initial Values



If you want to set specific starting values to ad-hoc values, you can edit `$theta` directly:



```{r}
# Set the fixed-effect intercept starting value to 10
dataProfile$theta$betaFE[1] = 10
```



## Redrawing Initial Parameters with `theta_init()`



To draw a fresh set of starting values from the prior—for example, to initialize a second independent MCMC chain—use `theta_init()`:



```{r}
print(paste("Old FE intercept parameter:", dataProfile$theta$betaFE[1]))

dataProfile$theta = theta_init(dataProfile$prior, dataProfile$params)

print(paste("New FE intercept parameter:", dataProfile$theta$betaFE[1]))
```



## Modifying Prior Hyperparameters



Finally, you can modify prior hyperparameters directly in `$prior` before running `profileGLMM_Gibbs()`. If you want the initial parameters to reflect the updated prior, call `theta_init()` again afterward:



```{r}
# Set a stronger penalty on the fixed-effect prior
dataProfile$prior$FE$lambda = 100

# Redraw initial values using the updated prior
dataProfile$theta = theta_init(dataProfile$prior, dataProfile$params)

# Check the updated initial fixed-effect parameters
print(dataProfile$theta$betaFE)
```
